correctness.rationale: Canonical proper-color block sequences biject with acyclic orientations; Hasse covers are exactly consecutive-block edges. The covering graph is a tree precisely when all interior blocks are singletons (with a two-block star exception). Tree signed-root vectors form an integral basis, and nontree cover graphs make the cone nonsimplicial. The closed formal matrix series sum all proper-color walks with endpoint nonempty blocks and intermediate singleton blocks; comparison with separately enumerated acyclic orientations passes five complete small cases. The proof, not finite experiments, establishes the universal claim.

originality.rationale: The pre-existing complete-bipartite graphical-zonotope smooth fixed-point enumeration and the general Postnikov–Reiner–Williams tree-poset criterion are explicit background, not new claims. A new arbitrary-color-count multivariate rational matrix enumerator for the regular fixed points of K_{a1,...,ar}, r>=3, is not supplied by the inspected general sources, indexed searches or recoverable previous-claim comparisons. An unindexed result for simplicial chambers of multipartite graphic arrangements could subsume it; the PASS is qualified.
residual_risks: A source using simplicial chambers, rather than toric fixed points, might already provide an equivalent general complete-multipartite count.
The generalization shares structural proof ingredients with the previously completed two-color case, though its all-color transfer matrix is not mathematically identical.

value.rationale: The complete multipartite family is a canonical parameterized class of toric varieties. The formula counts regular torus-fixed points for arbitrary numbers and sizes of vertex classes in a single computable rational matrix expression, beyond the pre-existing two-part count or unrestricted acyclic orientations. It provides exact geometry-sensitive data for potentially singular fans without constructing their full face lattices; the K_{2,2,2} and K_{2,2,3} examples illustrate a genuine multicolor phenomenon.
